deviations.what: bf16 Qwen: per-token cosine >= 0.998 and the AGENTS.md drift criterion instead of the spec's per-token cosine >= 0.999
deviations.why: Neither implementation meets the spec's per-token threshold in bf16: torch bf16 (SDPA on MPS, as the pipeline loads Qwen) has 4 of 602 tokens below 0.999 (worst 0.99844), MLX bf16 has 3 (worst 0.99852); only one token is below in both. The float32 MLX path matches the float32 reference at rel_l2 <= 2.3e-5, so the port is exact. Likely causes, from the analysis in validation: (1) bf16 keeps 8 mantissa bits, and rounding in the residual stream accumulates over 28 layers to rel_l2 about 1.5e-2, i.e. a mean token cosine near 0.9999 with a tail; (2) a per-token minimum over about 600 tokens is an extreme-value statistic, much stricter than the global cosine of AGENTS.md (about 0.9996-0.9999 here, which passes); (3) the sensitive tokens are a property of the model: the per-token errors of torch and MLX correlate at 0.63-0.89 and their worst tokens coincide (a lone space before a digit, '1', ';', 'orbit', the Cyrillic 'зам' of 'замедленная'); (4) which of those tokens crosses 0.999 then depends on kernel details that differ between the two implementations (Metal kernels of MLX's fused SDPA, RMSNorm and matmuls vs torch MPS kernels: accumulation order and where intermediates are rounded), while the precision policy is the same (RoPE angles in float32 with cos/sin cast to bf16, RMSNorm in float32, softmax in float32 inside SDPA): MLX bf16 and torch bf16 differ from each other by rel_l2 1.2-2.0e-2, as much as each differs from float32. The criterion used instead: AGENTS.md (rel_l2 <= 2 x torch bf16 drift per prompt) and per-token cosine >= 0.998. Downstream, even float32 instead of bf16 embeddings move a Smoke video to 23-26 dB PSNR (quantization study), so a 0.999 vs 0.998 token cosine has no visible effect on its own. Users who want the reference-exact embeddings can encode in float32 (--qwen-dtype float32, 28 GB peak).

deviations.what: the float32 Qwen reference is computed layer by layer, not by one Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGeneration call
deviations.why: float32 7B needs about 30 GB; one layer at a time needs about 4 GB. A tiny-model test shows the streamed forward equals the pipeline's full call on padded input with its mask (rel_max <= 1e-5).

deviations.what: the torch bf16 drift is recorded on Apple MPS with SDPA attention
deviations.why: an earlier attempt with eager attention gave token cosines of 0.27-0.87: eager rounds the large Qwen attention logits to bf16 before the softmax. The pipeline loads Qwen with from_pretrained's default SDPA, so SDPA is the representative basis. torch bf16 on the CPU was not used as a basis (report 05/09: bf16 on this CPU is not representative).

deviations.what: the text cache keeps only the real tokens (no padding, no mask)
deviations.why: as decided in spec 09: right padding cannot change real-token states under causal attention, and report 05 shows the DiT output is unchanged; CLIP padding cannot reach the pooled position either

deviations.what: Qwen weights in the tests and runs come from the ComfyUI single-file copy, not the checkpoint's text_encoder shards
deviations.why: no 15.5 GB download; all 729 tensors have the shards' names, shapes and dtypes, the 368 small ones are byte-identical and the 361 large ones match in their first and last 4 KiB (validation). The shard route used by the HF card's quick start was not run.

architecture_notes.note: Qwen bf16 encodes the 238-token Smoke prompt in under a second after a ~5 s load; the peak is 13.4 GB (weights 15.2 GB in bf16 are mostly the 152k x 3584 embedding and 28 layers). CLIP-L is negligible.
architecture_notes.optimization: 8-bit Qwen: 9.1 GB peak with embeddings as close to float32 as bf16's. Encode, free, then load the DiT (done).

architecture_notes.note: Even float32 instead of bf16 embeddings (rel_l2 1.5e-2 between them) changes a Smoke video to 23-26 dB PSNR; 8-bit embeddings stay at that level (23.3-26.6 dB), 6-bit and 4-bit drop to 20.6-22.6 dB on one prompt, and 4-bit changes face details visibly.
architecture_notes.optimization: Judge text-encoder changes on embeddings (rel_l2, token cosine) and by eye, not by video PSNR alone.

architecture_notes.note: 8-bit Qwen: supported (embedding rel_l2 2.9e-2 = 1.09x bf16's, video PSNR at the float32-vs-bf16 level). 6-bit (rel_l2 8.6e-2, worst token cosine 0.84) and 4-bit (0.22, 0.34): not supported.
architecture_notes.optimization: The 16 GB profile (spec 14) can use 8-bit Qwen.

architecture_notes.topic: bf16 precision of Qwen2.5-VL-7B text states
architecture_notes.note: Final hidden states have norms of 250-350 per token; bf16 rounding over 28 layers gives rel_l2 about 1.5e-2 vs float32 in both torch and MLX, concentrated on a few context-sensitive tokens (whitespace, digits, punctuation, rare subwords). An earlier attempt with eager attention in bf16 gave token cosines down to 0.27: rounding the large attention logits to bf16 before the softmax is far worse than SDPA.
architecture_notes.optimization: Keep SDPA-style attention with float32 softmax (mx.fast.scaled_dot_product_attention does); if text fidelity ever matters more, encode in float32 (only once per prompt, ~1 s) — memory, not speed, is the cost.
